requiredFindingDispositions.finding: RC-1 does not determine resolutionCompleteness.state for unresolved-edge@observed.
requiredFindingDispositions.independentAssessment: The contract-clarity gap is real: RC-1's list named seven one-rung relations and syntactic rungs, which leaves unresolved-edge@observed and types@annotated undetermined. The reference host, by contrast, already decided applicability by membership in the five resolved rungs, so the divergence the blind review measured is between two readings of the PROSE, not between the prose and the model.
requiredFindingDispositions.correction: RC-1 now states complete applicability over the registered (relation, rung) pairs of the single ladder authority: the rule is membership of the RUNG in the closed five-member resolved set, never ladder length. The five resolved pairs are enumerated and may never claim not-applicable; the remaining twelve, including unresolved-edge@observed and types@annotated and every syntactic rung, are not-applicable with attempted=false, count 0 and empty classes. reachability@from-resolved-calls is called out as the one-rung relation that is nevertheless resolved. An unregistered pair refuses and not-applicable is never a fallback. RC-2 state and the examined-versus-resolution distinction (RC-3) are preserved verbatim in substance.
requiredFindingDispositions.notDone: No generic one-rung count rule was used. No fallback state was created for unknown records.
requiredFindingDispositions.citedEvidenceLimitation: The blind vector rc1-unresolved-edge-state-gap.json retains only two payload digests and admitted flags. The two admissible records it compares necessarily differ in `attempted` and `stageTerminal` as well as in `state` (complete requires attempted=true / stageTerminal=complete; not-attempted requires attempted=false), so 'the same observation' is stronger than the retained evidence exhibits. That limitation does not dissolve the contract gap, which is about which state RC-1 determines, and the correction is made on the gap.

newFindings.title: admit_coverage_result_v3 does not re-check ladder membership of the entry's own (relation, rung) pair
newFindings.measured: A cross-relation pair whose rung is registered for a different relation - unresolved-edge@resolved-binding - ADMITS at the Coverage producer boundary when its resolutionCompleteness is a resolved-shaped record, and mints a coverage2. It is caught later at use, where sufficiency_v2 resolves no ladder index and reports required-relation-missing, and it is refused at fact admission. An UNREGISTERED relation or rung refuses at that boundary on the schema enum.
newFindings.whyNotFixedHere: Adding a membership check at the producer boundary is a behaviour change to the reference host, outside this correction's minimal contract/schema-description scope, and none of the four required findings depends on it.
newFindings.effectOnThisCorrection: The RC-1 replacement was written to NOT overclaim: it says an unregistered value refuses on the schema enum and that a cross-relation rung is refused at fact admission and resolves no ladder index at use. It does not claim the Coverage producer boundary refuses cross-relation pairs.

Every observation here is over reference models and synthetic fixtures. No compiler, cargo, provider, repository, filesystem, ledger or renderer was executed, and nothing here is product qualification.
My reference controls exercise the reference host models in this subject. Where a control 'refuses', that is the reference model applying the stated rule, not evidence about any implementation.
